- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use moving average of prior 5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.3.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period prices (last 5–7 days); adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 forecast points if sentiment is neutral or rising.
- If sentiment is high and price is near 80+, model often fails to account for mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 2–3 periods if price > 82.
